answers.text: Answered with one new item that holds three complete drafts of Tool 1, one for each strategy: call:civ/chapters/14_ch14.md:a69db048:note/tool1-three-strategies. (a) The question put before the event: one question asked of the partisan before the outcome, with the failed prophecy (Festinger, Riecken, and Schachter, 1956) and the double-blind test of astrology (Carlson, Nature, 1985) as examples. (b) The believer taken out of the observation, and each excuse examined as a claim: the N-rays, from Wood's letter to Nature of 1904, then a four-step procedure and the Single Ledger. (c) Your six points kept word for word, with two real comparisons for points 4 and 5: Korea at night (NASA) and East Germans leaving for the West before the Wall. All three carry your sentence about God: a belief may be sealed about God; only how it treats reality is examined. The chapter is unchanged. Left to you: which strategy, whether the six points survive as the procedure, and the term hermetic belief, which is yours and is now defined in the first paragraph. Sources and checks: ext-ref/tool1_hermetic/report.md.

Answered with a new item: call:civ/chapters/13_ch13.md:14d51098:note/red-green-through-cases. The list of five is gone. Four cases are told in order, and each ends with the idea it gives: London 2004, Tower Hamlets 2014, Lewisham 2016, Paris 2019. Your block quotation is kept word for word and moved to the end as the conclusion; then three things that hold the sides together, where the cooperation breaks, and your four questions. Alternate b is the same without the passage on the two sacred claims. Every quotation is from the sources saved for the earlier draft, and no new fact was added. The chapter is unchanged. Left to you: whether the block quotation moves to the end, whether the heading changes, and whether the passage on the sacred claims stays.

Answered with a new item: call:civ/chapters/08_ch08.md:9547789f:note/two-situations. COVID is gone. One situation takes its place: Hurricane Katrina in 2005, where the agency paid two thousand dollars on the applicant's word before any inspection, and the Government Accountability Office estimated that about one payment in six rested on an identity, an address, or a claim that was false or filed twice (GAO-06-844T). The agency disputed the size of the estimate and accepted most of the recommendations for checking applicants (GAO-06-1013). Then the point about kindness and your two closing sentences. Alternate b adds one situation for your sentence on public order: the House of Commons committee on the August 2011 disorder. The first paragraph is the one you called good. The chapter is unchanged. Length fell from 619 words to 342 (a) and 374 (b). Sources: ext-ref/kindness_politeness/report_round2.md.
